program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s target and criterion are broadly aligned with the request, and the traces show genuine progress: the edit is desaturated and has a grainy, sketch-like appearance, but retains photographic detail and some color. The disagreement is mainly a threshold ambiguity: several traces treat muted tones and pencil-like texture throughout as complete, while another explicitly distinguishes those cues from a fully rendered drawing. Tighten the typed criterion so “complete” requires a consistently hand-drawn pencil appearance across the image, not merely global desaturation or a texture overlay; reserve “partial” for visible drawing-style progress that still reads substantially as a photograph. Keep “absent” and “unknown” distinct, and require evidence to cite both drawing-specific marks/shading and any remaining photographic regions. Do not change the binding or force the reference label: the reference constrains the aggregate, while the image evidence supports investigating this completion boundary. All traces are valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport or schema failure; their high confidence despite divergent labels suggests calibration/criterion ambiguity rather than insufficient coverage.
